idiom_name: one base handler (template method) that runs the shared security sequence before the action's business step
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define exactly one handler skeleton - an abstract base type, a dispatch wrapper or an equivalent template method - through which every presentation action is invoked, and place the security sequence inside it: establish or verify identity, authorize the operation, validate the session, verify or canonicalize input, and record the audit event, in that order. The skeleton calls the concrete action's business step only after every check passes, translates failures into one error contract, and stays free of per-operation policy so that the enforcers remain the only place policy lives. Whatever the platform calls the entry point (front controller, router, middleware chain, dispatch table), make it the only path to an action and treat a bypass - direct handler registration, internal invocation, batch entry - as a defect, because the pattern's guarantee is completeness, not best effort.
pitfalls: Coverage, not structure, is the guarantee: an action reachable without passing through the base silently loses every check.
A base that grows one overridable hook per concern spreads the policy surface across subclasses; keep the template final and delegate the mechanisms.
Order is part of the contract: authentication before authorization, session validity before session-dependent decisions.

Wrong move: the base grows session plumbing, role tables and error rendering because it is the one shared class everyone can reach -> the security sequence becomes a god object that is risky to change and every presentation action inherits the blast radius of each edit -> keep the base thin: sequence plus failure translation only, delegate each mechanism to a dedicated enforcer.

Wrong move: ship a skip/exempt escape hatch (skip_before_action, a per-action opt-out flag) and let public or convenience endpoints use it -> exceptions accumulate until the base covers a shrinking fraction of the surface and complete mediation quietly lapses -> default the gate to fail-closed, make exemptions central, declared and reviewed, not per-action.

Wrong move: force every action to inherit the security base when actions already extend a framework-supplied class -> single-inheritance languages have no room left, teams copy the checks inline or grow a second parallel hierarchy -> realize the same choke point as mixins, filters or middleware wrapped around the dispatcher where the platform only allows one parent.
